speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs (a) what does Singapore consider the key priorities for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) in its relations with the United States (US) under the new Trump administration, bearing in mind the US President's absence from ASEAN summits during his first term as President; and (b) what messages will Singapore convey to its US counterparts during the ASEAN country dialogues and at the East Asia Summit under the chairmanship of Malaysia.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
text: The US' presence in our region has in fact underpinned our peace, stability and prosperity in Southeast Asia for many decades.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
text: The US has been an active supporter of ASEAN and this includes strengthening collaboration in new growth areas, for instance artificial intelligence (AI), cyber security and energy transition.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
text: The omni-directional engagement on the part of ASEAN towards the US, to China, to the EU, to India, to Australia and indeed all the middle powers, and our emerging links with Africa and South America, is an essential element of ASEAN's vision for an open, inclusive and rules-based regional architecture in our region.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
text: We believe this is the way to secure peace and prosperity, and also based on the appreciation of the fact that in contrast to many parts of the world, Southeast Asia remains at peace and has good prospects for significant growth in the decades to come.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
text: In this respect, the US' commitment to the ASEAN Outlook on the Indo-Pacific, which they have expressed on previous occasions, is reaffirmation of this point.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
text: We will keep emphasising the mutually beneficial nature of ASEAN's interactions and engagement with the US.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
text: So, the point here is that this is a mutually beneficial relationship.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
text: ASEAN's rapidly developing economies present significant opportunities for American companies including areas like critical minerals, energy, manufacturing, technology, including digital and AI.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
text: The US' presence in the region, both economically and therefore also having interests to protect from a defence perspective, has been crucial to maintaining stability and opportunities in our part of the world.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
text: From an ASEAN perspective, the primacy of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Seas (UNCLOS), which sets out maritime entitlements, and avenues for peaceful resolutions of disputes, and sets out as a right freedom of navigation and overflight, is crucial for ASEAN, both from a stability point of view as well as economic prospects for the future.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
text: So, Mr Speaker, we will continue to work with our partners in ASEAN to seek opportunities for high-level engagement with the new US administration on this basis.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Does the Minister and envisage a role for ASEAN or Singapore in the peace negotiations that hopefully will get underway very soon, similar, to the way we made an effort to bring the US and North Korea together a few years ago?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There are far more proximate partners and stakeholders in the dispute, in the conflict between Ukraine and Russia, than Southeast Asia.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Having said that, let me give a Southeast Asian perspective.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If you look at the votes of the 10 ASEAN member states, you will find that all of us, in our votes and in our explanation of votes at the UN, have emphasised the importance of the UN Charter and the principles of sovereign equality, political independence and territorial integrity.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: ASEAN, perhaps also because of our past experience in the Cold War, has absolutely no intention of allowing ourselves to be a future arena for proxy wars and we will certainly have no intention to allow ourselves to be caught in the strategic contestations between superpowers in the future.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Bear in mind, ASEAN's prospects for the future.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Bear in mind, our adherence to international law in the UN Charter.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And just as importantly, bear in mind, our prospects for the future.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Both of us emphasised economics – so trade, investments, energy.
